- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–20% of the spike magnitude for next 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 72+ to 65–68), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a “first 5 days discount” — reduce forecast by 5–10% for first 5 days of 30d output.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +1.0 to -0.5), model may lag in adjusting; apply a “sentiment lag correction” — shift forecast 1–2 days backward to align with sentiment shift.
